note: Written by Claude from reputable outlets (Reuters via syndication partners, ABC News, Al Jazeera, The Standard, Yahoo Finance and others); source under each story. Singapore, Southeast Asia, Japan, South Korea and China sections are shorter because fewer reputable reports could be retrieved this morning. Sports excluded.

items.headline: Chip stocks crash 12% as AI trade unravels
items.summary: The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 12.25% on Thursday, with AMD down about 15% and Nvidia and Micron among the hardest hit, as large-cap tech had its worst day since the Covid sell-off. Nomura's Charlie McElligott blamed hedge funds locking in 2026 profits rather than any sudden change in fundamentals; investors are also weighing whether a Democratic Congress will slow AI data-centre buildout.

items.headline: Palantir sheds about $40bn in value as software sinks
items.summary: Palantir lost roughly $40 billion of market value in a day, and security names including CrowdStrike, Cloudflare, Okta and Palo Alto Networks also fell sharply. Salesforce and Adobe were little changed.

items.headline: Tesla and SpaceX both drop more than 9%
items.summary: Shares of Tesla and SpaceX each fell over 9% on worries about regulatory hurdles to a possible merger and to data-centre expansion under the new Congress.

items.headline: AppLovin jumps on revenue beat
items.summary: AppLovin shares surged about 23% before the open after third-quarter revenue of $2.18 billion beat expectations of $2.07 billion. Qualcomm, by contrast, slid after its results.

items.headline: Canva to cut more than one in five jobs
items.summary: Australian design-software company Canva announced it will cut over a fifth of its workforce, with its chief executive calling it the hardest moment in the company's 13-year history.

items.headline: Wall Street's post-election rally collapses; Nasdaq in correction
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 4.36% to 7,353.73, the Dow lost 1,833 points (3.44%) and the Nasdaq dropped 5.52%, entering correction territory. The VIX jumped nearly 70% to 28.18, and the Dow was on track for its worst second session after a midterm since 1896. Retail investors were net sellers of about $358 million, per Vanda Research.

items.headline: Bank of England hikes to 4%, its first rise since 2023
items.summary: The BoE raised Bank Rate a quarter point to 4% on an 8-1 vote, with Catherine Mann wanting a half-point move. It sees inflation near 5% by mid-2027 and warned at least one more hike is likely if the US-Iran conflict continues.

items.headline: Oil rebounds as Iran-deal hopes waver; gold edges up
items.summary: WTI rose 3.2% to about $91 and Brent traded near $98 amid uncertainty over whether President Trump will pursue a deal to end the Iran war, after Vice President Vance linked the midterm losses to the conflict. Gold gained 0.7% to $4,100.

items.headline: Bitcoin slides below $76,000
items.summary: Bitcoin fell more than 5% to under $76,000 after topping $80,000 on Wednesday, with the market still digesting last week's $6.3 billion Binance hack. Stifel said the crypto Clarity Act is unlikely to advance before year-end.

items.headline: 3M agrees up to $7.35bn PFAS settlement
items.summary: 3M will pay up to US$7.35 billion to settle claims over PFAS groundwater contamination; Australia's separate A$2 billion Federal Court case against the company continues.

items.headline: DBS third-quarter profit falls 5%, missing forecasts
items.summary: Singapore's largest bank reported net profit of S$2.81 billion, down from S$2.95 billion a year earlier, as trading income slumped even though net interest income rose. DBS warned of uncertainty from high energy prices, higher rates and geopolitical risk.

items.headline: Haze season winds down; masks and shelters end Saturday
items.summary: NEA says inter-monsoon showers have cut the risk of transboundary haze to low. Mask distribution and haze shelters close at 6pm on 7 November, and MOH will end the haze subsidy schemes from 12 November. Friday's PSI is forecast in the moderate range.

items.headline: Indonesia's growth beats forecasts at 5.47%
items.summary: Indonesia's economy expanded 5.47% year on year in the third quarter, above the 5.18% expected in a Reuters poll, led by manufacturing including palm-oil processing for biodiesel. The central bank called domestic demand resilient.

items.headline: Anwar campaigns in Melaka ahead of state polls
items.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim heads to Melaka on Friday for five engagements, including Pakatan Harapan campaign events. The state votes on 14 November, with early voting on 10 November.

items.headline: Mekong states meet in Beijing; Vietnam and China agree to speed rail links
items.summary: At the 11th Lancang-Mekong foreign ministers' meeting, Vietnam's Le Hoai Trung urged stronger regional links and joint work on non-traditional security threats. He and Wang Yi agreed to accelerate three railway projects; China set out five proposals including AI and disaster-warning cooperation.

items.headline: Takaichi pledges continued cooperation with Trump
items.summary: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi declined to comment on the US midterm results, calling them an internal matter, but stressed the alliance remains a central pillar of Japan's diplomacy and security.

items.headline: Nikkei falls for a fourth day as chip stocks slide; Toyota soars
items.summary: The Nikkei 225 lost 1,110 points (1.79%) to 61,077.90, dragged by Advantest, Tokyo Electron and SoftBank Group. Toyota jumped 16.7% after raising its profit forecast.

items.headline: Beijing attacks Japan's new security documents
items.summary: China's foreign ministry called Tokyo's revised security strategy and defence spending 'remilitarisation', saying the label of China as Japan's greatest strategic challenge is a pretext for military expansion.

items.headline: Kospi plunges 5.3% as chipmakers tumble
items.summary: The Kospi closed at 5,383.80, with SK hynix down 9.46% and Samsung Electronics down 7.57%, as fears grew that a Democratic Congress could tighten rules on AI data centres and dent chip demand.

items.headline: Seoul to move anti-piracy unit closer to Hormuz
items.summary: The defence ministry will seek parliamentary approval to extend the Cheonghae unit's Middle East mission and shift it to waters near Oman's Duqm port, about 650km from the strait, adding a P-8A patrol aircraft and 75 personnel, after US pressure to support the Iran war.

items.headline: North Korea fires missiles, rejects talks with Washington
items.summary: Pyongyang fired several missiles into the sea off its east coast, hours after denying US claims that its hackers stole more than $6 billion from Binance. Kim Yo Jong ruled out dialogue until Washington drops its 'hostile policy'.

items.headline: David Jones collapses into administration
items.summary: The 188-year-old department store chain called in administrators after falling behind on rent and failing to reach a deal with Westfield owner Scentre, its biggest landlord. Its 38 stores keep trading under receivers while a sale or recapitalisation is pursued, and the network is expected to shrink.

items.headline: NAB profit falls 13% as bad-debt charges jump
items.summary: NAB's full-year cash profit fell 13.4% to $6.14 billion, with credit impairment charges up 86% to $1.55 billion. It held its dividend at 85 cents and shares fell about 7.5%.

items.headline: Woodside to cut at least 500 jobs
items.summary: Woodside Energy plans to cut about 10% of its global workforce to save $550 million a year from 2028; most of its staff are in Western Australia.

items.headline: NextDC soars 49% on surprise stake raid
items.summary: A vehicle co-owned by Goodman Group and Digital Realty bought NextDC shares at $9.50, targeting up to 9.9%. NextDC's board called the move opportunistic and said no takeover proposal had been received.

items.headline: ASX 200 rallies 2.6%; Bendigo lifts mortgage rates
items.summary: The ASX 200 closed up 2.61% at 9,065.1 on post-midterm optimism, though energy stocks fell. Bendigo Bank will raise variable home loan rates by 0.25 points after the RBA's fifth hike this year took the cash rate to 4.85%.

items.headline: Democrats head for biggest House majority since 2008
items.summary: By Thursday afternoon Democrats held 251 House seats to 155 for Republicans, and 54 Senate seats to 44, having flipped seven Senate seats, according to AP tallies.

items.headline: Mississippi and Alaska Senate races still too close to call
items.summary: Democrat Scott Colom led Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith by 1,724 votes with 96% counted; Mississippi has no recount law and certification runs to 13 November. In Alaska, Mary Peltola led Senator Dan Sullivan by 637 votes amid a dispute over a second 'Dan Sullivan' on the ballot.

items.headline: Jeffries launches speaker bid; Democrats play down impeachment
items.summary: Hakeem Jeffries announced his run for speaker, with Katherine Clark and Pete Aguilar seeking the next two leadership posts unopposed. Democrats say they will focus on costs and accountability rather than impeachment.

items.headline: Trump backs Hegseth publicly amid replacement reports
items.summary: Trump said Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is doing 'a very good job', but CBS and Fox News reported he is privately weighing a replacement, with Florida Governor Ron DeSantis floated.

items.headline: Melania Trump hosts Ukrainian and Russian officials
items.summary: The first lady hosted officials from both countries at the White House ahead of talks in Abu Dhabi aimed at ending the war. Trump also agreed the Iran war was a factor in the midterm defeat.

items.headline: Import expo opens as surplus heads past $1.2 trillion
items.summary: The 9th China International Import Expo opened in Shanghai with 4,142 companies from 162 countries. Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang called claims that China is squeezing out other economies 'completely unfounded'.

items.headline: Joshua Wong jailed for 10 years for foreign collusion
items.summary: Hong Kong's High Court sentenced the former Demosisto leader after he pleaded guilty to conspiring to collude with foreign forces. Beijing backed the ruling and told outside parties not to interfere.

items.headline: Beijing seeks 'strategic stability' with US after midterms
items.summary: China's foreign ministry called the midterms a US domestic matter and said Beijing will work with Washington to build a constructive, stable relationship. It declined to comment on SoftBank's reported bid for ABB's robotics unit.

items.headline: Hang Seng jumps 3.7% as Hong Kong wealth hits record
items.summary: The Hang Seng rose nearly 900 points, led by tech and gold stocks. A survey put Hong Kong private wealth at a record HK$12.9 trillion in 2025, up 24%.

items.headline: Sensex and Nifty post biggest gains in over a year
items.summary: The Sensex rose 2.6% to 79,310 and the Nifty 2.4% to 24,536.6, a sixth straight gain, as lower oil and hopes for US-Iran diplomacy lifted sentiment; autos and financials led. The rupee firmed to 94.475 per dollar.

items.headline: Cabinet extends Agniveer service by two years
items.summary: The Union Cabinet approved a two-year extension for Agniveers, opening a route to regular military service; the Indian Express says it covers 75% of recruits.
items.source: The Hindu; Indian Express (via NextIAS digest)

items.headline: Supreme Court questions two-child norm laws
items.summary: The court said falling fertility has made laws penalising breach of the two-child norm outdated, and referred its 2003 ruling to a larger bench.
items.source: The Hindu; Indian Express (via NextIAS digest)

items.headline: Government weighs ending safe harbour for social media
items.summary: The Centre is considering scrapping the legal immunity social media platforms enjoy for user content.

items.headline: ₹17,500 crore scheme to boost energy storage
items.summary: The government approved a ₹17,500 crore programme to promote energy storage systems, while India said it has secured $400 billion in renewable investment commitments.
items.source: Indian Express; The Hindu (via NextIAS digest)
